executive_summary: Bluspring’s September quarter demonstrates an accelerating mix shift toward higher-margin industrial services and acquisition-led scale. The investment case must reconcile the attractive ex-foundit presentation with much lower consolidated profits, and test whether acquisition and working-capital funding translate into durable shareholder cash flow.
research_stance: Improving operating trajectory, with consolidated cash conversion and acquisition discipline the key conditions.

thesis_drivers.title: Mix shift can improve economics
thesis_drivers.evidence: Smart Infra, Energy and Engineering reported a 10.9% EBITDA margin, versus 4.7% in facilities and food services and 3.2% in security. A higher contribution from industrial services can lift group profitability, but integration and ramp-up remain important risks.
thesis_drivers.source: September 2026 local financials and latest earnings-call transcript

thesis_drivers.title: Organic and inorganic growth must be separated
thesis_drivers.evidence: The call reports 49% YoY revenue growth excluding foundit, versus 16% growth in the existing business. Acquisitions explain much of the gap; total growth should not be treated as fully organic or free of capital requirements.
thesis_drivers.source: September 2026 local financials and latest earnings-call transcript

thesis_drivers.title: Excluding foundit does not eliminate the cost
thesis_drivers.evidence: The call emphasises PAT of ₹32 crore and EBITDA of ₹67 crore excluding foundit. Local consolidated PAT is ₹13 crore and operating profit ₹54 crore. Foundit losses and reporting-basis differences remain part of the valuation until the business is sold, closed or turned around.
thesis_drivers.source: September 2026 local financials and latest earnings-call transcript

industry_context.heading: Contract service economics
industry_context.content: Facilities, security, engineering and food services differ in margin, labour intensity and working capital. Revenue growth without contract-level returns or collections is not value creation.

industry_context.heading: Acquisition strategy
industry_context.content: STEAG and LSG bring industrial and aviation-food capabilities. LSG consolidated from August, so future comparisons must separate new scope from organic growth.

industry_context.heading: Macro read-through
industry_context.content: Infrastructure and industrial investment can expand demand, but wage inflation, financing costs and customer payment delays can severely affect thin-margin contracts.

cycles.name: Valuation Cycle

valuation.method: Segment EV/EBITDA and normalised consolidated cash flows; target deferred
valuation.assessment: The positive 102 x snapshot P/E is not reconciled with approximately −₹0.16 accumulated localEPS over the latest four quarters, and cannot anchor valuation. Use segment operating earnings and consolidated shareholder cash flow, explicitly including foundit funding and acquisition/working-capital debt.
assumptions: The FY27 guide of revenue above ₹4,700 crore, EBITDA above ₹200 crore and PAT of ₹100 crore was discussed on the basis excluding foundit.
A consistent bridge from ex-foundit operations to consolidated earnings is required before a target.
No assumption that working-capital debt is zero at year-end or that acquisition growth is capital-free.

bull: Industrial services mix and LSG integration lift margins without collection slippage.
Foundit losses fall and consolidated profit converges with core performance.
Acquisition debt is repaid from cash while high-return growth continues.
base: Organic growth is healthy but reported growth slows as acquisition comparisons normalise.

Valuation requires normalised consolidated earnings rather than best-segment multiples.
bear: Acquisitions fail to integrate or higher margin contracts demand larger working capital.
Foundit losses and borrowing costs offset core EBITDA growth.
Low contract margins leave equity profits sensitive to wages, collections and interest.

results_analysis: September 2026 (Q2 FY27), consolidated local financials report PAT of ₹13.0 crore versus ₹4.0 crore a year ago and ₹-2.0 crore in June 2026. The business includes loss or near-zero comparison periods; percentage profit growth is not an appropriate standalone signal.

Revenue ₹1,272.0 crore was +48.4% YoY and +34.0% QoQ. Local operating profit ₹54.0 crore and OPM 4.2% should be interpreted on the dataset’s definition, rather than automatically equated with management’s adjusted EBITDA or EBIT.

Smart Infra, Energy and Engineering reported 10.9% EBITDA margin against 4.7% facilities/food and 3.2% security. Growing the higher-value vertical can lift group profitability, but integration and ramp-up risks remain.

The local snapshot is dated 2026-11-13; cleaned-price technicals are dated 2026-11-12. The financials were read from the existing local lake. No replacement result-PDF figures or old overlay targets were silently substituted, and no post-refresh verification is claimed.

Scope reconciliation: management’s core numbers exclude foundit and comprise revenue of ₹1,250 crore, EBITDA of ₹67 crore and PAT of ₹32 crore. The local consolidated figures are ₹1,272 crore revenue, ₹54 crore operating profit and ₹13 crore PAT. These differences require a reporting-scope and metric-definition bridge; they are not automatically an operating beat or an accounting error.

Recognized foundit revenue of ₹22 crore, not its ₹30 crore sales/bookings, bridges core revenue ₹1,250 crore to the local ₹1,272 crore group revenue. Core EBITDA ₹67 crore less foundit loss ₹12 crore gives about ₹55 crore versus local operating profit ₹54 crore; residual rounding/definition remains. CorePAT ₹32 crore versus group ₹13 crore still needs a tax, financing, minority and adjustment bridge.

business_economics: The strategy is moving toward energy/industrial services, where current EBITDA margin 10.9% exceeds facilities/food 4.7% and security 3.2%. Better mix can create value, but contract mobilisation, wage pass-through, collection and safety execution still determine cash returns.

Revenue growth 49% excluding foundit is materially acquisition-assisted: existing businesses grew 16%. LSG consolidated only from August, making future annualisation meaningful but not free. The investor needs acquired-cohort earnings, integration costs and cash returns on consideration, rather than treating the entire growth rate as organic.
earnings_quality: The revenue bridge is more specific than a generic scope warning:₹1,250 crore ex-foundit core revenue+₹22 crore recognized foundit revenue=₹1,272 crore local group revenue. The separate ₹30 crore foundit sales figure is bookings/sales, not recognized revenue.

CoreEBITDA ₹67 crore less foundit EBITDA loss ₹12 crore gives approximately ₹55 crore, close to local operating profit ₹54 crore. CorePAT ₹32 crore versus group ₹13 crore needs further tax, financing and attribution work. The guide of ₹100 crore FY27 PAT belongs to the core basis, so it cannot be directly placed under a consolidated P/E.
capital_allocation: Management disclosed ₹340 crore acquisition consideration, acquired cash of roughly ₹188 crore and debt supporting both acquisitions and working capital. The intended ₹150 crore year-end acquisition debt is different from average ₹150–200 crore working-capital funding, which can remain even if a closing organic debt number looks low.

Foundit’s H1₹26 crore and H2₹12–13 crore outlook refer to EBITDA burn. Statutory cash requirements can differ. Loans of about ₹106 crore against a Board limit near ₹150 crore show a measurable funding exposure, but the approval is not proof that the turnaround will cost no more.
valuation_logic: The positive 102 x snapshot P/E conflicts with approximately −₹0.16 accumulated localTTM EPS and is not a usable earnings anchor until its adjustment/scope is explained. A segmentSOTP should include core recurring earnings, the cost/funding of foundit and financing needed for working capital.

A defensible acquisition-return analysis requires purchase consideration net of genuinely accessible cash, integration cost, incremental maintenance investment and cash conversion by acquired cohort. No target is asserted from the current core presentation alone.
peer_positioning: SIS and Updater Services offer useful comparisons for security/facilities execution, but their geographic, manpower, acquisition and service mixes differ. Quess is affected by the demerger perimeter and is not automatically a directly comparable historical group. A peer multiple must use consistent EBITDA, leases, debt and minority treatment.
